chunks: What al-Shaykh informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Wudu (ablution) is two by two; whoever adds to it will not be rewarded for it.” And he described to us the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so he washed his face once, and his forearms once, and he wiped his head with the remaining moisture of his wudu (ablution), and his feet.

His relating the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as once for each act indicates that by his statement, “Wudu (ablution) is two by two,” he meant the sunnah (prophetic practice), because it is not permissible for the obligation to be twice while the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would perform it once by once. And that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.السُّنَّةَ: the sunnah (prophetic practice), as distinct from the obligatory component
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.بِفَضْلِ وَضُوئِهِ: with the remaining moisture of his wudu (ablution)
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْهِ: his forearms, the arms washed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.لَمْ يُؤْجَرْ عَلَيْهِ: he will not be rewarded for it, indicating no reward for adding beyond the prescribed form
key_terms.مَثْنَى مَثْنَى: two by two, meaning twice for each washing
key_terms.مَسَحَ: he wiped, referring to the prescribed wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: his face, one of the parts washed in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: In Shia hadith, is wudu (ablution) performed once or twice for each limb?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the manner of performing wudu (ablution), reporting both the wording that it is done "two by two" and the practical example of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله performing the obligatory washing once each. It indicates a juristic distinction between what is obligatory in wudu (ablution) and what belongs to the sunnah (prophetic practice), making it significant for Shia fiqh discussions on ritual purity.
